title: The score's chords appear as named locators; the key as the set's scale
description:
As a producer, I want the chords shown in the set's timeline, so that I can see the harmony while I finish the piece.

```gherkin
Feature: Chords as locators
  Background:
    Given the sample "horn.wav" with a steady beat at 100 BPM

  Scenario: A locator at every chord change, named with the chord
    Given the score "c.apr" with the chords "I7 IV7 I7 . | IV7 . I7 ." in F
    When I export "c.apr" as a DAW set
    Then the set has locators at bars 1, 2, 3, 5, 7
    And the locators are named "I7 (F7)", "IV7 (Bb7)", "I7 (F7)", "IV7 (Bb7)", "I7 (F7)"

  Scenario: A split bar gets a locator mid-bar
    Given the score "c.apr" with the chords "[ii V] I" in C
    When I export "c.apr" as a DAW set
    Then the set has locators at bar 1 beat 1, bar 1 beat 3 and bar 2 beat 1

  Scenario: A score with no chords has no locators
    Given the score "c.apr" with "bars 4" and no chords
    When I export "c.apr" as a DAW set
    Then the set has no locators

  Scenario: The set's scale is the score's key
    Given the score "c.apr" in "F mixolydian"
    When I export "c.apr" as a DAW set
    Then the set's scale is F mixolydian
```

Note: locator names are the compiler's own chord labels (`ChordSpan.label`, e.g. `I7 (F7)`), the same text `apricity explain` shows. The scale scenario follows the decisions in `design/daw-set.md` (M0); the scale scenario is dropped if the target DAW version has no set scale.
